title: Truman's impossible atomic calculus
gist: David Vaiani reviews James M. Scott's 'Empire of Ashes', which details the horrors of Hiroshima and Nagasaki alongside Truman's painstaking decision process and Japan's strategic obduracy. Vaiani highlights Japan's misjudgement that democracy would not tolerate a long war, rejects the 'intimidate the Soviets' thesis, and leans toward the view that a prolonged war would have been worse.

insights.claim: After Pearl Harbor, Japan's leaders assumed democracy would hamper the US because voters would not tolerate a long and costly war, a misjudgement that contributed to Japan's downfall.
insights.speaker: David Vaiani
insights.so_what: Autocracies betting on democratic war-weariness can badly misjudge resolve, a recurring geopolitical risk pattern.
